# Finding ∫ 2x⁵ sin(x) dx

## Method: Tabular Integration by Parts

I'll use the tabular method, differentiating the polynomial and integrating the trig function.

| Sign | Derivatives of 2x⁵ | Integrals of sin(x) |
|------|-------------------|---------------------|
| +    | 2x⁵              | -cos(x)             |
| -    | 10x⁴             | -sin(x)             |
| +    | 40x³             | cos(x)              |
| -    | 120x²            | sin(x)              |
| +    | 240x             | -cos(x)             |
| -    | 240              | -sin(x)             |

## Multiplying along the diagonals:

$$+ (2x^5)(-\cos x) = -2x^5\cos x$$
$$- (10x^4)(-\sin x) = +10x^4\sin x$$
$$+ (40x^3)(\cos x) = +40x^3\cos x$$
$$- (120x^2)(\sin x) = -120x^2\sin x$$
$$+ (240x)(-\cos x) = -240x\cos x$$
$$- (240)(-\sin x) = +240\sin x$$

## Verification

Differentiating the result:
- d/dx[-2x⁵cos(x)] = -10x⁴cos(x) + 2x⁵sin(x)
- d/dx[10x⁴sin(x)] = 40x³sin(x) + 10x⁴cos(x)
- d/dx[40x³cos(x)] = 120x²cos(x) - 40x³sin(x)
- d/dx[-120x²sin(x)] = -240x sin(x) - 120x²cos(x)
- d/dx[-240x cos(x)] = -240cos(x) + 240x sin(x)
- d/dx[240sin(x)] = 240cos(x)

All intermediate terms cancel, leaving **2x⁵ sin(x)** ✓

<answer>-2*x**5*cos(x) + 10*x**4*sin(x) + 40*x**3*cos(x) - 120*x**2*sin(x) - 240*x*cos(x) + 240*sin(x) + C</answer>
